nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Summer light drives growth in the park forests and in the algae of its lakes.

nodes.name: Lakes and clear water
nodes.desc: Rainy, Kabetogama, Namakan and Sand Point lakes make up a large share of the park and hold its fish, algae and loon nesting waters.

nodes.name: Fire
nodes.desc: The park service describes fire as a long-standing force that renews forests, which are managed today with fire, forest health and visitors in mind.

nodes.name: Thin soil on ancient rock
nodes.desc: The park sits on very old Canadian Shield bedrock, with glacial scours and deposits shaping where soil and water collect.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead wood, leaves, carcasses and lake sediment, returning nutrients to soil and water.

nodes.name: Paper birch
nodes.desc: A pale-barked northern hardwood recorded in the park; browsed by deer, hares and beavers and a common pioneer after disturbance.

nodes.name: Balsam fir
nodes.desc: A boreal conifer of the spruce-fir forest type found in the park; eaten as browse by deer, hares and beavers.

nodes.name: White pine
nodes.desc: Once the dominant tree here, white and red pine were reduced by logging and few large mature stands remain.

nodes.name: Lowbush blueberry
nodes.desc: A low shrub with berries eaten by black bears and browsed by deer.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting microscopic algae that feed zooplankton at the base of the lake food chain. General ecology.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: Abundant in the park; browses birch, fir and pine and is a main prey of wolves and a common carcass for scavengers.

nodes.name: American beaver
nodes.desc: Feeds on birch, fir and pine and builds dams that reshape ponds and wetlands; the park service says beavers transform its ecosystems.

nodes.name: Snowshoe hare
nodes.desc: Browses young twigs and bark of birch, fir and pine, and is prey for wolves, bears and eagles.

nodes.name: American red squirrel
nodes.desc: A forest rodent recorded often in the park that eats conifer seeds and buds and is taken by eagles.

nodes.name: Water fleas (zooplankton)
nodes.desc: Tiny crustaceans that graze phytoplankton and feed small fish. General ecology.

nodes.name: Yellow perch
nodes.desc: A small lake fish that feeds on zooplankton and insects, and is prey for walleye and loons.

nodes.name: Walleye
nodes.desc: A top sport fish of the big lakes; adults eat mostly fish, often yellow perch.

nodes.name: Common loon
nodes.desc: Dives for fish, mostly small ones including perch and walleye; eggs and chicks are taken by eagles, and fluctuating water can flood nests.

nodes.name: River otter
nodes.desc: Hunts fish and waterfowl in the park lakes and wetlands.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A scavenger that feeds on carrion such as winter-killed deer.

nodes.name: Black bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats berries, deer, hares and beavers.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: The park top predator, hunting deer and also smaller prey like beaver and hares.

nodes.name: Bald eagle
nodes.desc: A fish-eating raptor that also takes loons, hares and squirrels and scavenges carcasses.
